blocks.html: Every chapter so far has assumed the data were trustworthy: a recorded weight, a recorded blood pressure, a recorded yes/no. Much Community Medicine research instead measures things no scale can read directly: satisfaction, quality of life, knowledge, stigma. This chapter asks two questions of any instrument: does it measure the right thing (validity, §16.2), and does it measure it consistently (reliability, §16.3, with agreement between two methods in §16.3.5)? It then links the two (§16.4), shows how items are compressed and combined into scores (§16.5–16.6), and ends with the full validation workflow (§16.7). No later analysis can repair a poor instrument: garbage in, garbage out.
